-- Message-ID makes the email channel idempotent: a re-delivered message is not registered twice
-- and continues from the step it reached.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS doc
),
inserted AS (
    INSERT INTO inbound_messages (
        message_id,
        source_type,
        from_address,
        from_name,
        subject,
        received_at
    )
    SELECT
        doc ->> 'message_id',
        doc ->> 'source_type',
        doc ->> 'from_address',
        doc ->> 'from_name',
        doc ->> 'subject',
        (doc ->> 'received_at')::timestamptz
    FROM input
    ON CONFLICT (message_id) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id, status
)
SELECT id AS inbound_message_id, status, TRUE AS is_new FROM inserted
UNION ALL
SELECT m.id, m.status, FALSE
FROM inbound_messages m
WHERE m.message_id = (SELECT doc ->> 'message_id' FROM input)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted);

UPDATE inbound_messages
SET
    source_text = $1::jsonb ->> 'source_text',
    attachments = $1::jsonb -> 'attachments',
    status = 'TEXT_READY',
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'inbound_message_id')::bigint
  AND status = 'RECEIVED'
RETURNING id AS inbound_message_id, status;

SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(m)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                id,
                message_id,
                from_address,
                from_name,
                subject,
                received_at,
                status,
                source_text,
                attachments,
                extraction,
                extraction_attempts,
                last_error,
                updated_at
            FROM inbound_messages
            WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'inbound_message_id')::bigint
        ) m
    ) AS message;

-- Claim one LLM attempt as a lease. EXTRACTING keeps any other run (for example a duplicate
-- delivery of the same email) from calling the LLM for this message at the same time;
-- recovery turns an expired EXTRACTING into FAILED. Counting attempts bounds retries.
UPDATE inbound_messages
SET
    status = 'EXTRACTING',
    extraction_attempts = extraction_attempts + 1,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'inbound_message_id')::bigint
  AND status IN ('TEXT_READY', 'FAILED')
RETURNING id AS inbound_message_id, extraction_attempts;

-- The extraction is stored once; later runs validate it again instead of calling the LLM.
UPDATE inbound_messages
SET
    extraction = $1::jsonb -> 'extraction',
    llm_model = $1::jsonb ->> 'llm_model',
    llm_usage = $1::jsonb -> 'llm_usage',
    status = 'EXTRACTED',
    last_error = NULL,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'inbound_message_id')::bigint
  AND status = 'EXTRACTING'
RETURNING id AS inbound_message_id, status;

-- Technical error of one LLM attempt (API error, timeout, malformed output). Recovery retries it.
UPDATE inbound_messages
SET
    status = 'FAILED',
    last_error = left($1::jsonb ->> 'error', 2000),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'inbound_message_id')::bigint
  AND status = 'EXTRACTING'
RETURNING
    id AS inbound_message_id,
    status,
    last_error,
    (SELECT NULLIF(value #>> '{}', '') FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'ops_workflow_id') AS ops_workflow_id;

-- Everything needed for one notification: client settings, the RFQ and its OPEN review
-- tasks that were not notified yet.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb ->> 'rfq_id' AS rfq_id
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(r)
        FROM (
            SELECT rfq_id, submission_id, customer_name, customer_email, subject
            FROM rfqs
            WHERE rfq_id = (SELECT rfq_id FROM input)
        ) r
    ) AS rfq,
    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object(
                    'id', t.id,
                    'line_number', t.line_number,
                    'review_type', t.review_type,
                    'payload', t.payload,
                    'access_token', t.access_token
                )
                ORDER BY t.line_number NULLS FIRST, t.id
            )
            FROM review_tasks t
            WHERE t.rfq_id = (SELECT rfq_id FROM input)
              AND t.status = 'OPEN'
              AND t.notified_at IS NULL
        ),
        '[]'::jsonb
    ) AS tasks;

-- Runs only after the email was sent: a failed send leaves tasks un-notified for a retry.
UPDATE review_tasks
SET notified_at = NOW()
WHERE id IN (
    SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb -> 'task_ids')::bigint
)
  AND notified_at IS NULL
RETURNING id;

-- A review link is valid only with the exact per-task token.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN $1::jsonb ->> 'task' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
             THEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'task')::bigint END AS task_id,
        $1::jsonb ->> 'token' AS token
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(x)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                t.id,
                t.rfq_id,
                t.line_number,
                t.review_type,
                t.status,
                t.payload,
                t.resolution ->> 'action' AS resolved_action,
                t.resolved_by,
                r.customer_name,
                r.subject
            FROM review_tasks t
            JOIN rfqs r USING (rfq_id)
            WHERE t.id = (SELECT task_id FROM input)
              AND t.access_token = (SELECT token FROM input)
        ) x
    ) AS task;

-- A review link is valid only with the exact per-task token.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN $1::jsonb ->> 'task' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
             THEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'task')::bigint END AS task_id,
        $1::jsonb ->> 'token' AS token
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(x)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                t.id,
                t.rfq_id,
                t.line_number,
                t.review_type,
                t.status,
                t.payload,
                t.resolution ->> 'action' AS resolved_action,
                t.resolved_by,
                r.customer_name,
                r.subject
            FROM review_tasks t
            JOIN rfqs r USING (rfq_id)
            WHERE t.id = (SELECT task_id FROM input)
              AND t.access_token = (SELECT token FROM input)
        ) x
    ) AS task;

-- Inbound emails whose extraction did not finish are retried from the stored source text.
-- Touching updated_at throttles repeated dispatch to once per grace period; the extraction lane
-- itself sends a message to manual handling after max_processing_attempts LLM attempts.
WITH cfg AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'processing_lease_minutes'), 10) AS lease_minutes,
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'recovery_grace_minutes'), 2) AS grace_minutes
),
-- Every run records it is alive; GET /webhook/health reports a stale heartbeat.
heartbeat AS (
    INSERT INTO system_heartbeats (name, last_seen_at)
    VALUES ('email_recovery', NOW())
    ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_seen_at = EXCLUDED.last_seen_at
    RETURNING name
),
expired_leases AS (
    UPDATE inbound_messages m
    SET
        status = 'FAILED',
        last_error = format('Extraction did not finish within %s minutes.', cfg.lease_minutes),
        updated_at = NOW()
    FROM cfg
    WHERE m.status = 'EXTRACTING'
      AND m.updated_at < NOW() - make_interval(mins => cfg.lease_minutes)
    RETURNING m.id, 'EXTRACTING'::text AS status
),
stuck_messages AS (
    UPDATE inbound_messages m
    SET updated_at = NOW()
    FROM cfg
    WHERE (m.status IN ('TEXT_READY', 'EXTRACTED', 'FAILED')
           AND m.updated_at < NOW() - make_interval(mins => cfg.grace_minutes))
       -- RECEIVED means ingest never stored the text; give a running ingest the full lease.
       OR (m.status = 'RECEIVED'
           AND m.updated_at < NOW() - make_interval(mins => cfg.lease_minutes))
    RETURNING m.id, m.status
)
SELECT id AS inbound_message_id, 'Inbound message stuck in ' || status || '.' AS reason
FROM stuck_messages
UNION ALL
SELECT id, 'Extraction lease expired.' FROM expired_leases;

parameters.content:
## Channel: Email
Command API: `{ operation, payload }`
- `ingest` — email from a mailbox source → text (body + PDF/XLSX/XLS/CSV) → stored checkpoint → extraction
- `extract` — `{ inbound_message_id }` → OpenAI structured output → deterministic validation → core `intake` / not an RFQ / manual handling email
- `notify_reviewers` — `{ rfq_id }` from the core → review email with links
Webhooks `GET/POST /webhook/rfq-review-form` — review form → core `review_decision`.
- `request_quote_approval` — `{ quote_id }` → customer email rendered once → approval email
- `send_quote` — `{ quote_id }` → deliver the approved email to the customer
Webhooks `GET/POST /webhook/quote-approval` — approval page → core `quote_decision`.
### Review form (links from the review email)

-- Everything needed to render, approve or deliver one quote. Looked up by quote_id, or by
-- quote_id + access_token for links opened by a person.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT
        $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id' AS quote_id,
        $1::jsonb ->> 'token' AS token,
        COALESCE(($1::jsonb ->> 'require_token')::boolean, FALSE) AS require_token
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(x)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                q.*,
                r.subject AS rfq_subject,
                r.submission_id,
                (
                    SELECT jsonb_build_object('name', c.name, 'discount_percent', c.discount_percent)
                    FROM customers c
                    WHERE c.customer_code = q.customer_code
                ) AS customer_account,
                (
                    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(qi) ORDER BY qi.line_number)
                    FROM quote_items qi
                    WHERE qi.quote_id = q.quote_id
                ) AS items
            FROM quotes q
            JOIN rfqs r USING (rfq_id)
            WHERE q.quote_id = (SELECT quote_id FROM input)
              AND (NOT (SELECT require_token FROM input) OR q.access_token = (SELECT token FROM input))
        ) x
    ) AS quote;

-- Store the rendered customer email once; an existing rendering is never replaced.
UPDATE quotes
SET
    customer_subject = $1::jsonb ->> 'customer_subject',
    customer_html = $1::jsonb ->> 'customer_html',
    customer_text = $1::jsonb ->> 'customer_text',
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE quote_id = $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id'
  AND customer_html IS NULL
RETURNING quote_id;

-- Everything needed to render, approve or deliver one quote. Looked up by quote_id, or by
-- quote_id + access_token for links opened by a person.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT
        $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id' AS quote_id,
        $1::jsonb ->> 'token' AS token,
        COALESCE(($1::jsonb ->> 'require_token')::boolean, FALSE) AS require_token
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(x)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                q.*,
                r.subject AS rfq_subject,
                r.submission_id,
                (
                    SELECT jsonb_build_object('name', c.name, 'discount_percent', c.discount_percent)
                    FROM customers c
                    WHERE c.customer_code = q.customer_code
                ) AS customer_account,
                (
                    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(qi) ORDER BY qi.line_number)
                    FROM quote_items qi
                    WHERE qi.quote_id = q.quote_id
                ) AS items
            FROM quotes q
            JOIN rfqs r USING (rfq_id)
            WHERE q.quote_id = (SELECT quote_id FROM input)
              AND (NOT (SELECT require_token FROM input) OR q.access_token = (SELECT token FROM input))
        ) x
    ) AS quote;

-- Runs only after the approval email was sent: a failed send leaves it for recovery.
UPDATE quotes
SET notified_at = NOW()
WHERE quote_id = $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id'
  AND notified_at IS NULL
RETURNING quote_id;

-- Claim delivery before the side effect. Only an APPROVED quote with a stored rendering can be
-- claimed, and only once: a second dispatch finds it SENDING and stops. If the run dies after the
-- email went out, recovery turns the expired SENDING into SEND_UNCERTAIN for a person to check.
UPDATE quotes
SET
    status = 'SENDING',
    send_attempted_at = NOW(),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE quote_id = $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id'
  AND status = 'APPROVED'
  AND customer_html IS NOT NULL
RETURNING quote_id;

-- Everything needed to render, approve or deliver one quote. Looked up by quote_id, or by
-- quote_id + access_token for links opened by a person.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT
        $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id' AS quote_id,
        $1::jsonb ->> 'token' AS token,
        COALESCE(($1::jsonb ->> 'require_token')::boolean, FALSE) AS require_token
)
SELECT
    (SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) FROM app_settings) AS settings,
    (
        SELECT to_jsonb(x)
        FROM (
            SELECT
                q.*,
                r.subject AS rfq_subject,
                r.submission_id,
                (
                    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(qi) ORDER BY qi.line_number)
                    FROM quote_items qi
                    WHERE qi.quote_id = q.quote_id
                ) AS items
            FROM quotes q
            JOIN rfqs r USING (rfq_id)
            WHERE q.quote_id = (SELECT quote_id FROM input)
              AND (NOT (SELECT require_token FROM input) OR q.access_token = (SELECT token FROM input))
        ) x
    ) AS quote;

WITH sent AS (
    UPDATE quotes
    SET status = 'SENT', sent_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW()
    WHERE quote_id = $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id'
      AND status = 'SENDING'
    RETURNING quote_id, rfq_id
)
UPDATE rfqs r
SET status = 'COMPLETED', updated_at = NOW()
FROM sent s
WHERE r.rfq_id = s.rfq_id
RETURNING s.quote_id, r.rfq_id, r.status;

-- The mail server reported an error: the email may or may not have left. A person decides;
-- the system never re-sends to a customer on its own.
UPDATE quotes
SET
    status = 'SEND_UNCERTAIN',
    notified_at = NULL,
    last_error = left($1::jsonb ->> 'error', 2000),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE quote_id = $1::jsonb ->> 'quote_id'
  AND status = 'SENDING'
RETURNING
    quote_id,
    status,
    last_error,
    (SELECT NULLIF(value #>> '{}', '') FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'ops_workflow_id') AS ops_workflow_id;
